abara2019.text:
Ownership and exit in municipal volunteer programs
Nkem Abara and Teresa Hollis (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 5]
We followed every volunteer who joined one of the programs in our panel during a single recruitment year and recorded the date of their last logged shift.

[p. 7]
Across the 48 programs in our panel, 31% of first-year volunteers exited before completing six months of service. Exit was concentrated in the first eight weeks.

brennan2016.text:
The Work Is Theirs
Siobhan Brennan (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 12]
Volunteers tend to exit once they no longer experience the work as theirs. Programs that hand volunteers a script and a schedule, and nothing to decide, see this most clearly.

castellanos2017.text:
Fit and retention in local volunteering
Rosa Castellanos and Kelechi Ibe (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 2]
We treat retention as a question of fit: whether the tasks a program offers match the goals a volunteer brings.

dumont2014.text:
Fixed-term assignments and volunteer re-enlistment
Claire Dumont (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 11]
Assignments with a clear end date made volunteers more willing to sign up again for a later assignment.

haldane2017.text:
Program size and attachment to staff
P. J. Haldane (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 21]
Volunteers in smaller programs reported stronger attachment to paid staff than volunteers in large programs.

iversen2018.text:
Peer mentoring in youth volunteer programs
Tor Iversen (SYNTHETIC)

Abstract. Youth volunteer programs that paired new volunteers with a peer mentor had higher retention at six months than programs without mentoring.

kessler2019.text:
Orientation length and volunteer retention
Dana Kessler (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 9]
Programs that reduced orientation to a single session saw twelve-month retention fall by 24% relative to programs that kept a multi-session orientation.

lindqvist2020.text:
Supervisor feedback and seasonal return
Hanna Lindqvist and Julia Morales (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 6]
The quality of supervisors' feedback predicted whether volunteers returned for a second season, net of program size and volunteer age.

marchetti2012.text:
Administrative traces of volunteer work
Paolo Marchetti (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 3]
This article studies the administrative traces of volunteer activity: sign-in sheets, shift logs, and incident forms. These records are kept for operational reasons and are rarely analyzed.

nakamura2020.text:
Recognition events and the long-serving volunteer
Emi Nakamura (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 15]
Recognition events had no measurable effect on exit among long-serving volunteers. If anything, exit rose slightly in the quarter after an event, a pattern we attribute to volunteers treating the event as a natural point to step down.

okafor2018.text:
Written role descriptions and volunteer tenure
Adaeze Okafor (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 4]
Volunteers who received a written description of their role remained active longer than volunteers who received only a verbal briefing.

quinlan2015.text:
Why volunteers say they leave
Maeve Quinlan (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 4]
In exit surveys, 37% of volunteers named scheduling conflicts as their main reason for leaving.

sorensen2022.text:
Coordinator turnover and volunteer exit (preprint)
Mikkel Sorensen (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 8]
Turnover among volunteer coordinators tends to precede spikes in volunteer exit by one to two months.

tanaka2016.text:
Training length and volunteer retention
Hiroshi Tanaka (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 19]
Once role clarity was accounted for, the length of training alone did not predict retention.

whitlock2020.text:
Named contacts and volunteer tenure in three cities
Grace Whitlock (SYNTHETIC)

[p. 112]
In two of the three cities, volunteers assigned a named staff contact stayed longer than those without one. In the third city the difference was small and not statistically significant.
